newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower, 2nd board falls back.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower, 2nd board falls back.

text.p: Share prices closed lower with speculative-driven second board stocks falling back after shooting past the 600-point mark in the morning, dealers said.
Blue chips drifted quietly throughout the day, consolidating after recent gains, they said.

"There's profit-taking in both main board and second board stocks but selling was quite well absorbed," said one institutional dealer. "I don't think the rally in second board counters is over. Interest is still very strong."
The blue-chip Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index ended down 1.01 points at 1,127.73.
The Second Board Index closed at 598.39, down 0.77, after hitting a new high of 607.08 in intraday trading.
Volume topped 372 million shares, with losers leading gainers 329 to 250.
Dealers said funds were digesting gains made in recent days and would probably stay out until the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee policy-making meeting next week.
"The market has not completely discounted a possible hike in interest rates," said a dealer.
